messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: likelihood
parts:
Xinya,

The information criteria are generally marginal, but you can get conditional by adding the argument "save.lvs=TRUE" to the model estimation command. Then some new metrics will appear in fitMeasures(), with "_cond" in their name. (And note that marginal are generally recommended.)

Ed

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: likelihood
parts:
Xinya,

The latent variables are assumed to come from a normal distribution, which is the same as non-Bayesian SEM. We might call the latent variable distribution a "hyperdistribution". Then, in a Bayesian model, the free parameters of the hyperdistribution (mean or variance of the normal distribution) would receive prior distributions. Those prior distributions can be found in dpriors().

Ed

messages.subject: Re: likelihood
parts:
Hi Ed,

I have a few follow-up questions about the likelihoods printed from blavaan. For a sample output below:

(n=150)
npar1  logl    ppp     bic     dic      p_dic    waic     p_waic   loo       p_loo    mlogl 
72 -2267.698 0.49825 4895.195 4676.975 70.78994 4681.485 71.05709 4682.442 71.53554 -2576.311

(1) Is the logl the same as the standard maximum likelihood when default priors are used ?
(2) Is the BIC reported equivalent to the BIC from ML estimation when default priors are used?
(3) What are the difference between logl and mlogl? BIC seems to be computed from the marginal likelihood logl as: BIC = -2*(-2267.698) + 72*ln(150) = 4896.162. Then how should I interpret mlog1?

Thank you so much!
Xinya




Xinya Liang

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: likelihood
parts:
Xinya,

The logl is the model log-likelihood calculated at posterior means.
The posterior means sometimes are close to the ML estimates, so these
log-likelihoods (and BICs) are sometimes similar. But there is no
guarantee here.

mlogl is the log-likelihood, marginalized over all parameters (via
Laplace approximation). This is the quantity involved in Bayes
factors.

Ed
